effects: Records the signer's vote For (1) or Against (0) on the given proposal; any other value reverts.
The vote counts with the signer's full governance vote power at the proposal's vote-power block, read from the GovernanceVotePower contract.
The vote is final: hasVoted is set and a second vote on the same proposal reverts. No tokens or native value move.
formats.shown: "cast vote" with the proposal id as a raw number and the support shown as For or Against.

findings.title: castVote: the proposal id is a 256-bit hash shown raw, so it does not say which proposal it is.
findings.evidence: GovernorProposals._getProposalId: uint256(keccak256(abi.encode(chainId, address(this), _targets, _values, _calldatas, _descriptionHash))); descriptor field 'Proposal Id' format raw. On chain, real ids are about 78-digit numbers.
findings.fix: No descriptor format can resolve a proposal id to its description. The label could say 'Proposal ID (hash)'.

findings.title: castVote has no interpolatedIntent, so the intent line leaves out the direction and the proposal.
findings.evidence: descriptor castVote: intent 'cast vote', no interpolatedIntent; the direction is only in the 'Support' field.

findings.title: castVote: the weight of the vote and that it cannot be changed are not shown.
findings.evidence: Governor._castVote: votePower = governanceVotePower.votePowerOfAt(_voter, proposal.votePowerBlock); GovernorVotes._storeVote: require(!_voting.hasVoted[_voter], "vote already cast").
findings.fix: The vote power is in storage and cannot be shown. A label or intent such as 'cast final vote' could say the vote cannot be changed.

findings.title: castVote tests use proposal id 42, which cannot be a real proposal id.
findings.evidence: cases/0.json and cases/1.json: data encodes proposalId 0x2a and the screen shows '42'. Real ids are keccak hashes.
findings.fix: Use a real proposal id taken from the chain.

formats.key: propose(address[] _targets, uint256[] _values, bytes[] _calldatas, string _description, (bool accept, uint256 votingStartTs, uint256 votingPeriodSeconds, uint256 vpBlockPeriodSeconds, uint256 thresholdConditionBIPS, uint256 majorityConditionBIPS, uint256 executionDelaySeconds, uint256 executionPeriodSeconds) _settings)
effects: Creates an on-chain governance proposal with the signer as proposer. Only a whitelisted proposer can call it.
Stores target calls (target, FLR value, calldata). If the vote succeeds, only the signer can execute them, by calling execute and paying the sum of the values in FLR.
Sets the voting terms: accept or reject type, voting start = max(now, votingStartTs), voting period, quorum threshold, majority, and a vote-power block picked at random within the vp block period.
Sets the execution window: start = voteEnd + executionDelay, pushed later to nextExecutionStartTime if needed, and length = executionPeriod. Later proposals are moved to after this window.
Nothing is paid now: the function is not payable and no tokens move.
formats.shown: "create proposal" with each target, its FLR value and raw calldata, the description, and all voting and execution settings.

findings.title: propose: the label 'Accept if vote passes' with a raw true/false hides what a reject-type proposal means.
findings.evidence: Governor._proposalSucceeded: when quorum or majority is not met it returns !_proposal.accept. With accept=false the proposal passes unless enough votes are Against. Descriptor: label 'Accept if vote passes', format raw, so the screen shows 'true'/'false'.
findings.fix: Relabel to 'Proposal type' and say what each value means, e.g. 'Accept-type (needs For majority)' / 'Reject-type (passes unless rejected)'. Use a map or a clearer label.

findings.title: propose: 'Values' in FLR reads as FLR sent now, but the signer pays it later when executing.
findings.evidence: PollingFoundation.propose is not payable. GovernorProposals._executeProposal: require(msg.value == sum, ...) runs at execute(), and Governor._execute requires proposal.proposer == msg.sender. Case 2 shows 'Values: 1 FLR'.
findings.fix: Label it 'FLR sent by each call on execution (paid by you)'.

findings.title: propose: proposal calldatas are shown as raw hex, so the actions being proposed cannot be read.
findings.evidence: descriptor field 'Calldatas' format raw on #._calldatas.[]; case 2 shows '0x12345678'. The calls are run later by the PollingFoundation contract, not in the signer's name.
findings.fix: Use format 'calldata' with calleePath #._targets.[] and amountPath #._values.[] where wallets support it.

findings.title: propose: some settings have special values that the screen shows literally.
findings.evidence: GovernorProposals._storeProposal: voteStartTime = Math.max(block.timestamp, _settings.votingStartTs), so 0 means now but would render as a 1970 date. execStartTime may be pushed to nextExecutionStartTime, which is in storage. 'Vp Block Period' does not say it sets the random vote-power block window.
findings.fix: Use labels such as 'Voting start (no earlier than)' and 'Vote-power snapshot lookback'.

findings.title: propose: the intent 'create proposal' does not say the proposal carries on-chain calls.
findings.evidence: descriptor intent 'create proposal' is used for both propose overloads; this one stores executable calls (executableOnChain = true when _targets.length > 0).
findings.fix: Use the intent 'create executable proposal' or add an interpolatedIntent with the description.

formats.key: propose(string _description, (bool accept, uint256 votingStartTs, uint256 votingPeriodSeconds, uint256 vpBlockPeriodSeconds, uint256 thresholdConditionBIPS, uint256 majorityConditionBIPS) _settings)
effects: Creates a text-only governance proposal with no on-chain calls, with the signer as proposer. Only a whitelisted proposer can call it.

Sets the voting terms: accept or reject type, voting start = max(now, votingStartTs), voting period, a random vote-power block within the vp block period, quorum threshold and majority. The execution delay is fixed at 0 and the execution period at 1.
Nothing is paid and no tokens move.
formats.shown: "create proposal" with the description and the voting settings.

findings.title: propose (text only): the label 'Accept if vote passes' with a raw true/false hides what a reject-type proposal means.
findings.evidence: Governor._proposalSucceeded returns !_proposal.accept when quorum or majority fails, so accept=false passes unless voted down. Descriptor: label 'Accept if vote passes', format raw.
findings.fix: Relabel to 'Proposal type' and say what each value means: Accept-type or Reject-type.

findings.title: propose (text only): 'Earliest voting start' of 0 means now but would render as a 1970 date.
findings.fix: Use a label such as 'Voting start (no earlier than; 0 = now)'.
